title: Nonsingular systems of equations over groups
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of Howie's conjecture: a finite system of equations over an arbitrary group G, in unknowns x_1, ..., x_n with coefficients in G, whose matrix of exponent sums has full row rank over Q, has a solution in some group containing G. Consequences: the Kervaire-Laudenbach conjecture (one equation with nonzero exponent sum) and the same statement for infinite systems with independent exponent rows. The first lesson states the theorem; the second sets up the rational cohomology of unitary groups with primitive generators compatible with block inclusions; the third proves that block unitary matrices in several unitary variables have simultaneous fixed spaces of total dimension at least the sum of the block sizes when the signed block counts have full row rank, by an intersection number computed from nested minors; the fourth proves the planar boundary obstruction for disk-and-band surfaces of several relator types with the spectral phase over the group von Neumann algebra; the fifth turns a relation into such surfaces with level arcs of several circle coordinates and removes them from the inside out.
prerequisites: programme course The Kervaire conjecture (the-kervaire-conjecture): lessons The regular trace and spectral phase (Lemmas 1.3, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1), A unitary with a large fixed space (Lemmas 1.1, 2.1, 5.1), Disks, bands and boundary words ((SURF), Lemmas 3.1, 4.2, 5.1, Theorem 2.1), The planar boundary theorem ((0.1), Lemma 3.1), From a relation to a planar surface (Lemmas 1.1, 3.1, 3.2, the extension of loops over disks)
programme course Poincaré duality on manifolds: lesson Poincaré duality, Corollary 2.1
programme course torsion-free-group-algebra-with-zero-divisors: the named statement (SURF) and the statement (PI1)

programme course Cell complexes, fundamental groups and covering spaces (cell-complexes-and-covering-spaces): lesson Fundamental groups of graphs and two-complexes, Corollary 2.4 and Theorem 3.3, which prove the statement (PI1)

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course: (UC) the rational cohomology of U(d) as an exterior algebra on generators of degrees 1, 3, ..., 2d-1 restricting along the standard inclusion (Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Corollary 4D.3(a)); (KU) the Künneth formula for products of compact manifolds with rational coefficients (Hatcher, Theorem 3.15); (INT) intersection numbers: the pullback of the Poincaré dual of p_*[R] evaluates to a signed count of transverse intersection pairs, zero for disjoint images, and duals of products are products of duals (Hatcher, Theorem 3.30; Hutchings, Cup product and intersections, Theorem 1.1) (lesson Rational cohomology of unitary groups, Section 1; Poincaré duality itself is proved in the programme course poincare-duality-on-manifolds); (REL) relations as maps of punctured disks, with possibly different loops on the holes (lesson From a kernel relation to a solution; Chen arXiv:2302.09811, Example 2.5; Hatcher, Section 1.1 and Proposition 1.26).

Named statement of another programme course used here: (SURF) surfaces in the sphere (course torsion-free-group-algebra-with-zero-divisors). The statement (PI1) on fundamental groups of 2-complexes, stated in that course, is proved in the programme course cell-complexes-and-covering-spaces (16 Oct 2026).
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
